what: Step 1: Fit the initial hazard models
title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: fit_initial() fits one hazard model per event process, expands data grid observed event times horizon tau, builds discrete state space targeting step works . process specified fit_types code delta column one-sided formula covariates hazard. processes can used covariates name, death hazard depends whether individual fallen ill (z). illness can occur , say individuals risk z z == 0. Exactly one process must censoring process (delta = 0). default hazards fitted Cox models. Setting fit = "hal" process’s entry uses highly adaptive lasso instead (experimental).
code: fit_types <- list(   z = list(     delta = 2,     model = ~L0,     at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0   ),   death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),   censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0) )  fit <- fit_initial(illness_death, fit_types = fit_types, tau = 1) fit$process_types #> $z #> [1] "one_jump" #>  #> $death #> [1] "terminal" #>  #> $censoring #> [1] "terminal"

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: tmle_alpha() estimates risk target process time tau intervention multiplies intensity z_name alpha. alpha = 1 intervention, observed risk death time 1: estimate contains targeted estimate tmle_est, standard error se, initial plug-estimate g_est. Halving intensity illness gives: 95% confidence interval follows standard error: Setting alpha = 0 removes illness altogether, alpha > 1 increases intensity.
code: observed <- tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", alpha = 1, z_name = "z") observed$estimate #>   tmle_est         se      g_est  #> 0.32504691 0.03906316 0.32504691 halved <- tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", alpha = 0.5, z_name = "z") halved$estimate #>   tmle_est         se      g_est  #> 0.30405495 0.03853505 0.31239982 est <- halved$estimate est[["tmle_est"]] + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * est[["se"]] #> [1] 0.2285276 0.3795823

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: calibrate_alpha() solves alpha achieves given exposure risk estimates target risk intervention. calibration target given exactly one : theta: risk z_name . rho: fraction observed risk z_name. delta: absolute difference observed risk z_name. rho_1a: fraction risk z_name opposite baseline treatment (see next section). example, risk death risk illness reduced 80% observed value: alpha_est calibrated intervention, theta exposure risk achieves, target_est risk death . standard error target_se accounts alpha estimated, whereas target_se_crude treats known.

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: baseline treatment A0, total effect treatment outcome can split part goes effect exposure remainder. calibrated intervention sets treated individuals’ exposure risk placebo, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total effect : mediated contrast: treatment versus calibrated intervention, calibrated contrast: calibrated intervention versus placebo. illness_death treatment, illustration add randomised treatment actual effect. treatment model given treatment_model, lists treatment values prepare estimates . contrasts computed influence curves fit returns. calibrated arm set = 1 rho_1a = 1, risk illness treatment calibrated equal risk illness placebo: treatment randomised without effect, confidence intervals three contrasts cover zero, expected.
code: set.seed(1) treated <- illness_death a0 <- rbinom(max(treated$id), 1, 0.5) treated$A0 <- a0[treated$id]  fit_treated <- fit_initial(   treated,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       delta = 2,       model = ~ L0 + A0,       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + A0 + z),     censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0)   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = A0 ~ L0,   a = 0:1 ) treatment_fit <- tmle_alpha(   fit_treated,   target = "death",   alpha = 1,   a = 1 ) placebo_fit <- tmle_alpha(   fit_treated,   target = "death",   alpha = 1,   a = 0 ) calibrated_fit <- calibrate_alpha(   fit_treated,   target = "death",   z_name = "z",   rho_1a = 1,   a = 1 )  calibrated_contrasts(treatment_fit, placebo_fit, calibrated_fit) #>    target   contrast   estimate         se       lower      upper #>    <char>     <char>      <num>      <num>       <num>      <num> #> 1:   <NA>      total -0.1405813 0.07724416 -0.29197704 0.01081449 #> 2:   <NA>   mediated -0.0234265 0.01632300 -0.05541899 0.00856599 #> 3:   <NA> calibrated -0.1171548 0.08141345 -0.27672220 0.04241266

title: Causal Inference for Multistate Event Processes via TMLE
text: pipeline three main steps: fit_initial() fits initial (nuisance) hazard models event process data, builds discrete product state space used internally. tmle_alpha() targets initial fit stochastic intensity intervention, scales intensity process alpha (optionally combined intervention baseline treatment). returns TMLE estimate, standard error, optionally efficient influence curve. calibrate_alpha() calibration_curve() calibrate intervention target effect size, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total treatment effect mediated calibrated contrasts. example, simulated illness-death data illness_death, illness z raises risk death, risk death time 1 intensity illness halved estimated : simulate multistate event history data, see simevent package.
code: library(MultiStateTMLE) fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       delta = 2,       model = ~L0,       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),     censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0)   ),   tau = 1 )  est <- tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", alpha = 0.5, z_name = "z") est$estimate #>   tmle.est         se      g.est  #> 0.30405495 0.03853505 0.31239982

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: data data.frame observed event history data long format, one row per event columns id, time delta (integer code process jumped, 0 reserved censoring), plus baseline covariates used fit_types. fit_types named list one entry per event process, named process. entry list elements: delta: process's integer code delta column data. Exactly one process must code 0 (censoring). model: one-sided formula covariates hazard model, ~ L0 + z. processes can used covariates name, case counting process (lagged one event) used. fit: "cox" (default) "hal". at_risk: optional function data returning logical vector, marking rows risk process (e.g. function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0 process can jump ). tau Positive number. Follow-horizon; target parameters evaluated tau. treatment_model Optional model baseline treatment, either formula A0 ~ L0 list elements model (formula) fit ("glm" supported). Required given. Optional integer vector baseline treatment values (0/1) compute interventional hazards clever weights . value can passed tmle_alpha(). max_count Positive integer. Maximum number jumps tracked per recurrent process state space. derived_vars Named list functions data deriving additional state variables. depend_time Named list functions describing dependence time since jump process, keyed process name. prune_states Logical. TRUE, prune states admissible at_risk functions fit_types. use_exponential Logical. TRUE, always transform hazard increments dH probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise done increments exceed 1. hal_control named list settings processes fitted fit = "hal", see Details. cores Positive integer. Number cores used parallel::mclapply() predicting hazards across states. verbose Logical. TRUE, print model fits progress.

title: Solve for the intervention achieving a target value — solve_alpha
code: # psi(alpha) = 0.6 * (1 - exp(-alpha)) has a known inverse, so # solve_alpha() should recover alpha = -log(1 - 0.3 / 0.6). fun <- function(alpha) {   psi <- 0.6 * (1 - exp(-alpha))   list(estimate = c(tmle_est = psi, se = 0.01), eic = rep(0, 10)) } res <- solve_alpha(fun, theta = 0.3, c_n = 1e-6) res$alpha_hat #> [1] 0.6931482 -log(1 - 0.3 / 0.6) #> [1] 0.6931472
